hero.headline: Indian River County sex sting nets 50 arrests, child-luring case highlighted
hero.teaser: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Thursday that law enforcement made 50 arrests during a four-day operation called Operation Late Checkout that targeted human traf
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Thursday that law enforcement made 50 arrests during a four-day operation called Operation Late Checkout that targeted human trafficking. Nearly all the arrests were for prostitution. Investigators also identified multiple individuals they believe are victims of human trafficking, and those investigations are ongoing.

 Flowers said the operation specifically targeted the trafficking of children and worked to capture people trying to lure children on the internet and meet up with them. Authorities pointed to the case of Carlos Reyes-Ayala, who is accused of traveling to Indian River County to meet with a child for sex.

 Flowers said investigators connected with many others seeking to exploit children during the operation. "We had a whole roomful of detectives that were chatting undercover with people who wanted to meet up with children. Our team was busy for days," Flowers said.

 Operation Late Checkout involved local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. "This operation shows that within our communities, there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it," said Special Agent Alphonso Williams of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

 Flowers said he expects more arrests to happen as a result of Operation Late Checkout. "It hurts our hearts when we see these cases and we see these kids. So, that's why we do these things," Flowers said.

cards.headline: Trail camera captures Florida panther mother with three cubs near Fort Myers
cards.teaser: A trail camera at a nature reserve in Fort Myers has captured new footage of a Florida panther mother with three young cubs, offering a promising sign for the endangered species' r
cards.body:
A trail camera at a nature reserve in Fort Myers has captured new footage of a Florida panther mother with three young cubs, offering a promising sign for the endangered species' recovery. The sighting is significant because it occurred farther north than where the endangered cats are usually seen in the state.

 Experts say the footage indicates the panthers are expanding their breeding range, which could help the population recover. Florida panthers are an isolated population of the North American cougar, a species of large, solitary wild cats that range mostly in western North America and most of South America. There are thought to be some 200 individuals living in southern Florida.

 Florida has spent decades trying to protect its panthers, primarily from encounters with cars and from a shrinking natural habitat. The cats' natural habitat has been reduced by about 95 percent from its original expanse.

 The trail camera video shows the mother and three young cubs moving through the Fort Myers nature reserve. The expansion of the breeding range north of their typical territory represents a potential turning point for a species that has faced severe population pressures from both vehicle collisions and habitat loss throughout southern Florida.

hero.headline: Indian River County sex sting nets 50 arrests, child-luring case highlighted
hero.teaser: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Thursday that law enforcement made 50 arrests during a four-day operation called Operation Late Checkout that targeted human traf
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Thursday that law enforcement made 50 arrests during a four-day operation called Operation Late Checkout that targeted human trafficking. Nearly all the arrests were for prostitution. Investigators also identified multiple individuals they believe are victims of human trafficking, and those investigations are ongoing.

 Flowers said the operation specifically targeted the trafficking of children and worked to capture people trying to lure children on the internet and meet up with them. Authorities pointed to the case of Carlos Reyes-Ayala, who is accused of traveling to Indian River County to meet with a child for sex.

 Flowers said investigators connected with many others seeking to exploit children during the operation. "We had a whole roomful of detectives that were chatting undercover with people who wanted to meet up with children. Our team was busy for days," Flowers said.

 Operation Late Checkout involved local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. "This operation shows that within our communities, there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it," said Special Agent Alphonso Williams of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

 Flowers said he expects more arrests to happen as a result of Operation Late Checkout. "It hurts our hearts when we see these cases and we see these kids. So, that's why we do these things," Flowers said.
